frameworks.name: Extended Marshmallow Test
frameworks.definition: A three-variable test of time-horizon and delayed gratification where the threshold window (waiting period for reward) is extended beyond standard 15-30 minute intervals to months or years, revealing true long-term orientation.

frameworks.name: 10-Stage Business Growth Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A structured progression from zero to $100M+ revenue with predictable stages defined by headcount increases, business function constraints, and symptom patterns; validated across software, physical products, services, and brick-and-mortar verticals.

claims.text: Your personal bar for excellence rises year-over-year as you accumulate experience; what you would have accepted as great work one, five, or ten years ago is substantially lower than your current standard.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Increasing obsession with quality on longer time horizons produces positive feedback that becomes addictive; spending an extra 50% of time on output yields proportionally more positive response.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Extended time investment and quality obsession compound positive feedback loops, creating intrinsic motivation to maintain higher standards.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi would not have been able to wait two years for a result ten years ago; the ability to delay gratification and maintain commitment despite uncertainty is a skill and muscle developed over time, not innate.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: The extended marshmallow test—where the reward-delay window is extended from 15-30 minutes to days, months, or years—more accurately predicts lifetime business success than the standard marshmallow test, because willingness to delay gratification on longer timescales correlates with greater total input investment.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Children (or people) who wait months for reward are willing to invest dramatically more total effort before receiving results, which compounds into superior outcomes across any domain.
bounded_by: The analogy breaks down at extreme intervals (e.g., asking a child to wait a month without food becomes a starvation scenario rather than a test of time preference).

claims.text: The 10-stage roadmap from zero to $100M+ is completed by less than 1% of companies; Alex Hormozi has executed it multiple times and can identify the stages with high confidence based on headcount milestones, business function constraints, and symptom patterns.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: validated across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar

numbers.axis: company completion rate of full roadmap

claims.text: Each stage of the 10-stage growth roadmap is characterized by eight distinct business functions, each with specific constraint symptoms and corresponding graduation steps that are consistent across verticals.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: across software, physical products, services, brick-and-mortar

examples.text: Hormozi spent two years writing and editing a book, aware throughout the process that it could flop, yet committed to the full timeline without cutting corners. This demonstrates the muscle of extended delayed gratification—willingness to invest substantial time with uncertain outcome.

Hormozi could not have committed to a two-year project ten years ago due to lack of developed time-horizon muscle; the ability to wait years for results is a learned capability, not a personality trait he always possessed.

practices.text: Develop your personal excellence bar by setting incremental quality targets; measure progress as your standard rises over months and years.
Extend your time horizon beyond immediate results; practice committing to longer projects (weeks, months, years) to build delayed-gratification muscle.
Visit acquisition.com/roadmap to download the 10-stage business growth roadmap from zero to $100M+; enter your information to receive the free framework.
Use the 10-stage roadmap as a diagnostic tool: identify your current stage by headcount and function constraints, then reference the symptom list and graduation steps for your vertical.
